meaning.en: To fail, be defeated, stop working, or come to an unsuccessful end.
meaning.zh: 失敗；遭到淘汰；停止運作；以失敗告終。

register.summaryEn: 語域及語氣 Bite the dust is an informal and vivid expression. It is common in conversation, journalism, sports commentary, entertainment and relaxed workplace discussion. It can carry a dramatic, humorous or slightly unsympathetic tone.
register.summaryZh: Bite the dust 是一個非正式而且形象鮮明的表達。 它常見於日常對話、新聞報道、體育評論、娛樂內容及較輕鬆的工作討論。
contextsEn: a machine that has stopped working
a product that did not succeed
register.formalZh: 在正式報告或學術文章中，直接使用以上中性表達通常更加合適。

benefits.zh: 你可以用一個簡短的慣用語，取代「計劃無法繼續，最後未能成功」這段較長的解釋。

benefits.titleEn: It Creates a Strong Mental Image
benefits.en: The image suggests that something has fallen so completely that it has reached the ground.
benefits.zh: 這個畫面令人想到某人或某事物完全倒下，甚至碰到地面的塵土，因此可以形象地表達徹底失敗。

benefits.en: a team; a business; a project; a machine; a device; a product. The exact Chinese translation should change according to the subject.
benefits.zh: 主語可以是計劃、想法、隊伍、企業、項目、機器、裝置或產品。 中文翻譯亦應按主語而調整，例如：

benefits.en: The first sentence expresses possibility. The second reports a completed failure.
benefits.zh: 這個項目已經失敗。 第一句表示可能性； 第二句則表示失敗已經發生。

examples.en: The project has bitten the dust.

benefits.titleEn: It Adds Energy to Informal Storytelling
benefits.titleZh: 令非正式敘述更有力量
benefits.en: The second sounds more vivid and dramatic, but it is also less formal.
benefits.zh: 第二句較為生動及有戲劇性，但語氣亦較不正式。

benefits.titleEn: It Develops Sensitivity and Register Control
benefits.titleZh: 培養語域及敏感度控制
benefits.en: Students learn that a memorable idiom is not automatically suitable for every serious situation. Use the expression for informal descriptions of failure, defeat or breakdown. Avoid it when respectful language is required.
benefits.zh: 學生可以學習到：容易記住或形象鮮明的慣用語，並不代表適合用於所有嚴肅情境。 這個表達適合非正式描述失敗、落敗或機器損壞； 需要尊重及慎重語氣時，則應避免使用。

origin.statusEn: Well-Documented Early Use; Exact First Spoken Use Unknown
origin.statusZh: 早期用法有較充分記錄；確切首次口語用法不明

history.en: Merriam-Webster dates its earliest known use to 1578. A report associated with a sixteenth-century battle described fallen bodies as lying on the ground and “biting the dust”. The surviving record shows that the early expression referred to violent defeat or death, although the date of its very first spoken use cannot be known.
history.zh: Merriam-Webster 把目前所知的最早用法追溯至1578年。 一份與十六世紀戰役有關的記述，以 「咬着塵土」的畫面形容倒在地上的人。 這項記錄顯示，早期意思與戰敗或死亡有關，但我們無法知道它最早在口語中出現的確切時間。

history.en: losing a competition; having a plan rejected; seeing a project fail; watching a business close; seeing a machine stop working.
history.zh: 這個原本描述戰敗者倒地的畫面，其意思後來逐漸擴展至：

origin.memoryEn: When something falls all the way into the dust, it has been completely defeated or has completely failed.
origin.memoryZh: 當某人或某事物徹底倒在塵土中，便可以聯想到它已完全落敗或失敗。

rules.zh: 冠詞 the 不可刪除或改成 a。

rules.titleEn: Use the Correct Irregular Verb Form
rules.titleZh: 規則二：使用正確的不規則動詞形式
rules.en: Correct target: bite the dust. Incorrect target forms: The plan bited the dust; The plan has bit the dust; The plan has bited the dust.
rules.zh: 使用正確的不規則動詞形式

rules.en: The plan will bite the dust yesterday.
rules.zh: 時間副詞 yesterday 要配合過去式 bit。

rules.titleZh: 規則四：保留情態及確定程度
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a possibility into a completed fact.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把「可能會失敗」改成了「已經失敗」。

rules.titleEn: Let the Idiom Replace the Failure Meaning
rules.titleZh: 規則五：讓慣用語取代失敗意思
rules.en: The second part repeats the meaning of the idiom. The reason remains, but the failure meaning appears only once.
rules.zh: 不要在使用慣用語後，再以 failed completely 重複相同意思。 銀行拒絕貸款後，計劃便宣告失敗。 原因獲得保留，但失敗意思只表達一次。

examples.en: The plan bit the dust when the bank refused the loan.
examples.zh: 銀行拒絕貸款後，計劃便宣告失敗。

rules.en: The weak answer removes the reason.
rules.zh: 較弱的答案刪除了咖啡店失敗的原因。

rules.titleEn: Match the Subject with the Chinese Meaning
rules.titleZh: 規則七：中文意思要配合主語
rules.en: Do not force one Chinese translation into every context.
rules.zh: 隊伍遭到淘汰。 咖啡店倒閉了。 打印機報銷了。 計劃宣告失敗。 不要把同一個中文譯法機械地套用在所有情境中。

rules.titleEn: Use It Only for a Real or Expected Failure
rules.titleZh: 規則八：只用於真正或預期的失敗
rules.en: The second sentence gives no evidence of failure.
rules.zh: 項目的資金耗盡後便宣告失敗。 第二句只說明項目開始，沒有證據顯示它失敗。

examples.en: The project bit the dust when its money ran out.
examples.zh: 項目的資金耗盡後便宣告失敗。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse Failure with a Small Problem
rules.titleZh: 規則九：不要把小問題當作徹底失敗
rules.en: A slow computer has not necessarily stopped working. The computer stopped working completely and could not be repaired.
rules.zh: 電腦短暫變慢，並不表示它已經報銷。 電腦完全停止運作，而且無法修理。

rules.titleZh: 規則十：小心處理真實死亡
rules.en: cold; humorous; disrespectful; violent; insensitive. The death meaning is not permitted in this exercise.
rules.zh: 這個表達可以表示死亡，但可能顯得冷漠、幽默化、不尊重、暴力或缺乏同理心。 本練習不接受死亡意思。

rules.titleZh: 規則十一：避免意外產生字面意思
rules.en: Only the second sentence contains the target idiom.
rules.zh: 孩子把泥土放進口中，用牙齒咬着塵土。 孩子的玩具車跌下樓梯後便報銷了。 只有第二句使用了本課的目標慣用語。

examples.en: The child put some soil in his mouth and bit the dust between his teeth.
examples.zh: 孩子把泥土放進口中，用牙齒咬着塵土。

examples.en: The child’s toy car bit the dust after it fell down the stairs.
examples.zh: 孩子的玩具車跌下樓梯後便報銷了。

rules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要在所有失敗情境中使用
rules.en: the document is highly formal; the topic is serious or sensitive; the precise type of failure matters; the reader may not understand informal idioms; a neutral tone is required.
rules.zh: 在高度正式、嚴肅、敏感或需要準確說明失敗類型的情況下，直接使用 fail、close、stop working 或 be defeated 可能更加合適。
